title: ph and wh, soft c and g; a whole sentence
cando: read a whole sentence, including the common words phonics cannot sound out

about.text: This is the last lesson of Letters & Sounds. You learn ph and wh, and the second sound of c and g. You learn common words that do not follow the sounds. Then you read whole sentences, from the capital letter to the full stop.
goals: Say the sound for ph and wh
Read c and g before e, i or y
Read the words that phonics cannot read
Read a whole sentence from left to right
Write a sentence with a capital and a full stop

chapters.title: ph and wh, and the two sounds of c and g
chapters.text:
This is Lesson 12. Two spellings and two letters.
First, ph. Look at it. P and h.
But it does not say p. It does not say h.
It says f.
Phone. ph. o_e. n. Three sounds.
Not p-hone. Fone.
Photo. Graph. All the f sound.
There are not many. Learn them as you meet them.
Next, wh. White. When. Where. Why.
It is very close to w on its own.
Most people say them the same now.
What matters is that you know it is one spelling.
And here is the useful part.
Nearly every question word starts with wh.
What. When. Where. Why. Which. Who.
See wh at the start and it is often a question.
Now the two letters. C and g.
You know c as in cat. That is the hard c.
But listen to this word. City.
City. The c says s.
Cent. Ice. Face. All the s sound.
When does that happen? There is a rule.
Before e, i or y, the c says s.
Cat, cup, cot. Hard c. A, u, o after it.
City, cent, cycle. Soft c. E, i, y after it.
Now g. You know g as in got. The hard g.
Listen. Age. Page. Giant.
The g says j.
Same rule. Before e, i or y, g often says j.
Only often. Get and give are hard.
So try the hard one, then the soft one.
One last thing about the letter y.
At the start it is a sound. Yes.
At the end of a short word it is long i. My.
At the end of a longer word it is long e.
City. Very. Happy. Only.
Three jobs for one letter.
One part left.

chapters.title: Reading a whole sentence
chapters.text:
This is the last part of Letters & Sounds.
There are no new spellings today.
You have every one of them.
Two things left. Then you are done.
The first is a short list of words.
These break every rule you have learned.
You cannot sound them out. Nobody can.
Would. Could. Two. Four. Because. People.
Look at would. W, o, u, l, d.
The l says nothing at all.
Look at two. T, w, o.
The w says nothing either.
People. That should be pee-oh-ple.
It is not. It is pee-pl.
There are about a hundred words like this.
A hundred, out of many thousands.
You learn them by sight, the way you did the.
And you meet them every single day.
So they come quickly.
Now the second thing. A whole sentence.
Until now you read words. One at a time.
A sentence is words in a line, with a job.
It starts with a capital letter.
It ends with a full stop.
Those two marks tell you where to start.
And where to stop and take a breath.
Read left to right. Always left to right.
Do not look ahead. Do not jump back.
If a word stops you, say its sounds.
Then go on. Do not start the line again.
Read the whole sentence. Then read it once more.
The second time is always better.
That is the last thing Letters & Sounds teaches.
And now you can read your Starter lessons.
Starter does not teach reading. It teaches English.
Your name. Your job. The time. A shop.
It asks you to read, and now you can.
Twelve lessons. Well done. Go on.

sounds.about: Two letters, one sound: f. Two letters that say the f sound.
Two letters, one sound: wh. It comes at the start of a word.
Before e, i or y, c says s: city, cent.
Before e, i or y, g often says j: age, page.

sentences.title: Write a sentence
sentences.lead: A sentence starts with a capital letter and ends with a full stop. Tap a sentence to hear it. Copy it on paper.
items: My phone is on the desk.

tricky.title: Words you learn by sight
tricky.lead: These words do not follow the sounds. Nobody can sound them out. Learn them by how they look. Tap to hear each one.

reader.title: The Phone Call
reader.text:
My phone rang at six.
It was a man from the city.
He said: when can you start?
I got on a white bus.
A wheel on the bus went flat.
I was late. The man did not care.

sentences.title: Five sentences
sentences.lead: Start at the capital letter. Read left to right. Stop at the full stop. Then read it once more.
sentences.text:
The shop is shut on Sunday.
I get the bus to work at eight.
My phone is on the desk.
The man said: wait here, please.
Two people came with me because the bus was late.

reader2.title: The First Day
reader2.text:
I would not say it was fun.
Two people came with me.
We were late because the bus did not stop.
The man at the gate had four names on a list.
He said: you are late, but go in.
I could read the list.
That was new, and it felt good.

readAloud.title: Reading check: 10 words
readAloud.lead: Record yourself reading these ten words. Then listen back, and tap each word to check.

sight.title: Reading check: sight words and a sentence
sight.lead: Now five words you learn by sight, and one sentence. Record yourself, then listen back.
items: The shop is shut on Sunday.

canDo: I can read words with ph and wh, and the soft c and g.
I can read common words that do not follow the sounds, like people and because.
I can read a whole sentence from the capital letter to the full stop.
I can write a sentence with a capital letter and a full stop.
